config.title: Default Configuration
config.intro: This app runs on one PC. Map the three folders every run needs, wherever they are on this PC. A runtime here uses them where they are; a pod carries them on its volume and links the paths the project's own files name onto them, so graphs and scripts run unchanged. The full story: docs/MOUNT-POINTS.md.
config.runpodHint: The account the app creates pods in.

config.apiKeyUnset: Not set. From runpod.io, Settings, API Keys; stored on this PC only, never shown again.
config.volumeHint: The datacenter, the network volume that carries the three folders, the image and the idle stop every new pod gets unless its own configuration says otherwise.
config.volumeIdHelp: This account's volumes in the chosen datacenter; picking one with no datacenter chosen sets the datacenter. Volumes in the navbar makes new ones.
config.mountPathHelp: Where the volume appears in the pod.
config.datacenterHelp: Must match the volume's datacenter. S3 marks the ones whose volumes take uploads with no pod running; the cards and prices are what a volume pod pays there (secure cloud).
config.imageHelp: What every new pod boots: ours, with the packs and the entrypoint that makes the links. It must be pushed to a registry first; a bare local name is refused at pod creation.
config.idleHelp: Stop a pod after this long with nothing queued. 0 = never.
config.syncParallelHelp: rsync streams at a time on a push, 1 to 16: one per top-level folder. The uplink is the limit; streams keep it full across thousands of small files.
config.foldersHint: The three every run uses, then any of your own; the exact links a pod makes are in the pod preview below. Mode {mode} (COMFY_MODE); {rule}

volumes.title: Network volumes
volumes.intro: A network volume is a disk in one RunPod datacenter that pods mount at /workspace. It bills whether or not a pod runs; a pod stopped on it bills nothing. Every pod the app creates attaches the Default Configuration's volume unless its own configuration names another.
volumes.none: No network volumes on this account.

volumes.createHelp: About ${cost} a month at 0.07 per GB. A volume only grows afterwards, never shrinks, and never leaves its datacenter. S3-marked datacenters take uploads with no pod running.

connect.intro: Accounts give the app access to private repositories; repositories attached here are what Attach node offers when creating a pod; MCP hands Claude, Codex or ChatGPT the pods and a ComfyUI.

adapters.hint: An adapter is a small JavaScript file that maps a package folder onto ComfyUI-Shared. Edit opens it in the Adapter Studio, built-ins included (editing a built-in makes an override; Reset undoes it). Duplicate copies one under a new id. There is no approval step; an adapter only ever runs fenced, with read access to the folder it is given and no write access.

import.title: Import Shot Pack
import.intro: Bring a package folder into this PC's ComfyUI-Shared through an adapter: the adapter reads the folder (it never changes it) and plans where each file goes; nothing is written until you press Import. Sync then puts ComfyUI-Shared on a pod or volume.

sync.title: Sync {name}
sync.unavailable: Sync runs in the app: the core copies over SSH from this PC. A plain browser build cannot.
sync.confirm: This copies between the folders mapped on this PC and the pod's network volume over SSH. Additive: nothing is deleted on either side. A first push of the whole tree can take hours at this PC's uplink; later ones send only what changed. The pod stays up and its idle stop is held until the copy ends; you can close this window and come back.
sync.push: Push: this PC to the volume
sync.pull: Pull: renders back to this PC
sync.plates: Include the plates (client material; needs a named yes)
sync.nothing: Nothing to copy: map the folders in Default Configuration first.
sync.finishedWarnings: Done: {steps} folders in step, {warned} with warnings; the output names the files rsync could not finish.
sync.failedSteps: {failed} of {steps} folders failed; the output says why.
sync.cancelled: Cancelled; what was copied stays, the next run resumes.
sync.background: Running in the app, not in this window: close it and come back any time. Cancel stops the copy; what landed stays.
sync.skipRendersHelp: The renders already made stay on this PC; the pod makes new ones. Pull is what brings renders back.
sync.planCountsWithout: {files} files, {bytes} with the skipped folders left out
sync.noCount: The count is not known in advance on this transport.
sync.listing: Listing {folder}: counting the files to copy…
sync.sharedHelp: Starts from this pod's Configuration (else the Default Configuration). Output is what pods write, so it is usually left behind. Anything else in the folder always goes.
sync.skipTestsHelp: Quick-test renders for his timeline; no shot's graph reads them. They stay on this PC.
sync.existingTitle: A file that is already on the pod
sync.existingHelp_update: Sends a file when its size or modified time differs; identical-looking files are skipped. The usual choice.
sync.existing_size: Skip the same name and size
sync.existingHelp_size: Fast. A file edited to the same size is not sent, whatever its time says.
sync.existingHelp_checksum: Compares the content of every file at both ends, so it is exact and slow: 16 GB is read twice.
sync.existingHelp_replace: Sends every file again and overwrites what is there.

mcp.intro: Two MCP servers come with this app: the pod manager (what the dashboard does) and the ComfyUI bridge (inside one ComfyUI). A client launches them with this app as its program, nothing else to install, or reaches them over HTTP while the app serves them. Pick a client below, copy its setup, and press Check to see the server answer from here.
mcp.notBuilt: Not built yet: run {command} in the app's folder.

mcp.claudeDesktopHint: Merge into claude_desktop_config.json (Settings › Developer › Edit Config), then restart Claude Desktop.
mcp.chatgptNote: ChatGPT only takes remote MCP servers: switch on Serve from the app above, tunnel that port from this Mac (ngrok, cloudflared), and give ChatGPT the public URL ending in /mcp under Settings › Connectors.
mcp.remoteHint: For any client that takes a remote MCP URL. The app serves it itself on this Mac only (127.0.0.1), with the app's own pods, sync and idle watch.
mcp.remoteOff: Switch on Serve from the app above to get this URL.

mcp.claudeCodeHint: Run in a terminal; the server is then on for every Claude Code session. The app itself is the program.
mcp.serveHint: Serve this endpoint over HTTP from the running app (127.0.0.1 only), so it uses the app's own pods, sync jobs and idle watch. Saved in Default Configuration; off by default.
